stories.title: Attenborough-backed appeal secures £30m estate
summary: The purchase of the vast Rothbury Estate by wildlife groups is hailed as "something very special".

stories.title: Fears for mature Scots Pines burned by huge Highland wildfire
summary: Experts say some older Scot pine damaged by fire could die removing an important source of seeds

stories.title: Physicists created a tiny universe and watched time emerge without a clock
summary: Scientists have created a miniature universe in the laboratory that could help answer one of the biggest mysteries in physics: What is time, and where does it come from?
Using 24,000 ultracold atoms, a University of Birmingham researcher built an isolated quantum system that repeatedly expands and contracts, mimicking the Big Bang and a possible Big Crunch.
Remarkably, the experiment showed that time could emerge from changes happening inside the system, without relying on an external clock.

stories.title: The asteroid killed the dinosaurs. Why did crocodiles survive?
summary: Scientists may have solved a 66-million-year-old mystery: how crocodiles survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs.
A sweeping analysis of fossils and ancient climates suggests that their preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that remained habitable even after the catastrophic impact.

stories.title: Hubble reveals a stunning twist in how the universe emerged from darkness
summary: A surprising discovery by astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope is challenging a leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from a dense fog of hydrogen roughly 13 billion years ago.
Scientists once believed powerful winds from exploding stars helped radiation escape galaxies and clear that cosmic fog, but new observations reveal that these winds actually block radiation instead.

stories.title: Scientists reveal a hidden snakebite crisis killing up to 513,000 people a year
summary: A startling new study suggests that venomous snakebites are killing far more people worldwide than official statistics indicate, with an estimated 274,000 to 513,000 deaths every year.
Researchers found that as many as 7 million people could suffer snake envenoming annually, while more than 800,000 survivors are left with long-term disabilities.

stories.title: What makes this golden eagle chick so important?
summary: The bird's arrival on a managed grouse moor in southern Scotland is seen as a key moment for the species.

stories.title: Hazardous driving conditions for Friday as fog warning issued by Met Office
summary: Foggy conditions likely to bring tricky conditions for the Friday morning commute as severe weather warning issued.

stories.title: Astronauts just gave the International Space Station a powerful upgrade
summary: Two astronauts completed a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk to install a new solar array on the International Space Station, bringing NASA one step closer to a major power upgrade.
Once the final array is installed on November 5, the station will have up to 30% more available power, supporting critical operations and its eventual controlled deorbit.

stories.title: Largest woodland bat survey a 'nice story of AI for good'
summary: Some of Britain's rarest and most threatened bats have been recorded in the south-west of England.

stories.title: Scientists confirm global warming is accelerating faster than ever recorded
summary: Earth is warming faster than ever recorded, with scientists detecting a major acceleration in global temperatures since around 2015.
A new study reveals that the warming rate has surged to approximately 0.35°C per decade, nearly double the average pace observed from 1970 to 2015.
After removing natural climate fluctuations, researchers confirmed the acceleration with more than 98% statistical confidence.

stories.title: A mysterious star system just 16 light-years away may be hiding habitable planets
summary: Astronomers have solved a 170-year-old planetary mystery in a nearby two-star system, discovering that a mysterious wobble was caused by stellar activity rather than a giant planet.
Although Jupiter-sized worlds have been ruled out in key regions, smaller, potentially habitable planets could still be waiting to be discovered just 16 light-years from Earth.

stories.title: Scientists discover mysterious seahorse lookalikes that no one has ever seen alive
summary: Scientists have discovered that three bizarre deep-sea fish that look exactly like seahorses actually belong to a separate evolutionary group, proving that nature created the same unusual body shape more than once.
Nicknamed "sea muppets," these elusive creatures are known from just seven specimens, and no one has ever seen one alive.

stories.title: Scientists discover why chronic back pain feels so personal
summary: A surprising discovery at UC San Diego suggests that chronic lower back pain may become deeply embedded in the brain's sense of personal identity.
Researchers found that movement-triggered pain activates a brain network associated with self-awareness and memories, even though ordinary acute pain typically shuts this network down.
This unexpected difference could explain why conventional pain medications often provide limited relief and why fear, anticipation, and past experiences can intensify chronic pain.

stories.title: Firefighters celebrate rain during Indonesia wildfires
summary: A number of clips show firefighters celebrating in the rain.

stories.title: A single brain signal may explain schizophrenia's most puzzling symptoms
summary: Scientists have identified a weakened brain signal that may connect several seemingly unrelated symptoms of schizophrenia, including sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity.
The surprising discovery could help explain the disorder's underlying mechanisms and potentially lead to earlier detection and new treatments.

stories.title: Six popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
summary: A study of nearly 13,000 adults found that people consuming the most artificial sweeteners experienced a 62% faster decline in memory and thinking skills, equivalent to approximately 1.6 additional years of brain aging.
Six popular sweeteners were linked to faster cognitive decline, raising concerns about the long-term brain health effects of common sugar substitutes, although causation was not established.

stories.title: A 700,000-year-old elephant tooth reveals a lost world where early humans lived
summary: A remarkably preserved elephant tooth dating back nearly 700,000 years has revealed a surprisingly lush prehistoric world where giant elephants and early humans lived side by side.
Discovered in northern Israel alongside ancient stone tools, the tooth belonged to a straight-tusked elephant, one of the largest land mammals of the Ice Age.

stories.title: NASA discovers Jupiter’s invisible shield is more complex than Earth’s
summary: NASA’s Juno spacecraft has discovered that Jupiter uses a surprisingly complex system of powerful plasma waves and multiple shock regions to defend against the solar wind.
The findings reveal major differences between Jupiter and Earth and could help scientists understand the enormous shock waves produced by exploding stars.

stories.title: Serious pollution by water industry remains high despite £5bn investment
summary: All but one of England's water companies were rated as "poor" or "requiring improvement" for environmental targets.

stories.title: Einstein's equations may explain the universe without dark energy
summary: Mathematicians have uncovered what they argue is a fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe, potentially challenging the need for dark energy.

Their calculations suggest that the mathematical framework used to describe cosmic expansion is inherently unstable and that the universe could accelerate naturally under Einstein's original theory of gravity.
The findings also raise surprising questions about whether our location in the universe is as ordinary as scientists have long assumed.

stories.title: Less than 42 minutes of bright daylight linked to higher dementia risk
summary: Getting more daylight could be linked to a surprisingly powerful benefit for brain health.

In a study of more than 87,000 adults, researchers found that higher daytime light exposure was associated with a 16% lower risk of dementia, with longer exposure to bright light linked to even greater reductions.
Remarkably, getting less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily was a stronger predictor of dementia than six established risk factors.

stories.title: 128,000-year-old ice in Tibet could rewrite climate history
summary: Ancient ice discovered high in Tibet may be more than 128,000 years old, preserving an extraordinary record of Earth's climate that scientists previously thought had been lost.
The discovery reveals a rare glimpse into the last ice age and could reshape our understanding of how glaciers survive dramatic changes in global climate.
